new_jobs.title: IT Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
CECO Environmental is a global leader in providing sustainable solutions for industrial air, water, and energy transition. Since 1966, we’ve been addressing the world’s most pressing environmental challenges. Our mission is to protect people, the environment, and industrial equipment, making a tangible impact across industries like renewable energy, semiconductor manufacturing, power generation, and water treatment. As a purpose-driven company, we foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, and integrity, ensuring that every project we undertake creates lasting positive change. At CECO, you’ll be part of a growing, dynamic team committed to a cleaner, safer, and more sustainable future.

We are proud to share that CECO was named one of Newsweek’s America’s Greatest Companies for 2025 and that Forbes recognized CECO as one of America’s Most Successful Small Cap Companies for 2026, marking our third consecutive year on the Forbes list. CECO Environmental is a publicly traded company on the NASDAQ under the ticker CECO, reflecting our strong growth, financial performance, and commitment to delivering value to shareholders.

The IT Program Manager will be responsible for IT Program Management for Business Enterprise Applications. This includes Dynamics 365 F&O and CE. In this role, you will be responsible for working with the ERP Teams to set and develop current workload and standards. You will plan for D365 Migrations from legacy ERP systems and D365 Enhancements. Another key responsibility is to oversee and ensure key milestones are met for each delivery. You will work and build the enterprise Business Applications roadmap. You will have active oversight to the work of multiple project managers. This role will report into the CECO IT PMO.

Specifically, the role owns two parallel mandates: planning and executing the migration from our current ERP to Dynamics 365 F&O and managing and planning for the D365 enhancement backlog. The scope of program management will also include the same activities for Microsoft Dynamics CRM— including continuous roadmap planning and prioritization.

You will operate under minimal supervision as a trusted member of the ERP program, working comfortably in an environment where requirements evolve and answers are not always predefined. Success requires a methodology mindset with flexibility and delivery focus. Someone who values structured, repeatable practices without letting process impede delivery.

This role will be onsite in Addison, TX.

Your Responsibilities Will Be

Corporate Business Applications Program Roadmap and Planning. You will partner the ERP system architecture leads to outline timing, approach and scope.
Develop and own integrated program plans, budgets, resource plans, risk registers, and status reporting for executive stakeholders.
The Program Manager will have accountability for the work performed by the project managers assigned to the migrations.
Each application migration or new system implementation will be subject to audit – both internal and external. As such, the Program Manager will be held accountable for adherence to “New System Implementation” controls.
Direct functional and technical workstreams (solution architects, consultants, developers, business analysts) across Finance, Supply Chain, and Operations modules, ensuring alignment with business process owners.
Manage third-party implementation partners and vendor engagements, including SOW scope control and quality assurance. Candidates must be comfortable with solving complex problems and understand how and when to escalate resource delivery issues.
Drive organizational change management, user training, and adoption so the business realizes value from day one.
The IT Program Manager will be exposed to M&A Integration activities. This includes working with acquired business workstreams to migrate acquired business applications, mainly focused on ERP migrations. The M&A Integration work will include fast paced business interactions to ensure alignment and coordination with business objectives while leading and communicating through change associated with M&A Integration activities, all while minimizing disruption to business operations.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree required (Business, Information Systems, Computer Science, or related field); Master’s degree a plus.
PMP, PgMP, Agile (SAFe/PSM) certifications a plus.
Microsoft Dynamics 365.
Experience in manufacturing, distribution, professional services industry with SOX hands on experience.
Background in both program-level governance and hands-on problem-solving (stepping into a workstream to unblock critical issues).
Experience managing budgets of and vendor/SI relationships.

ADA Requirements

Office Positions

Work Environment: This position is based at the headquarters located in Addison, TX. Minimal physical requirements, primarily computer use, and communication via virtual platforms, are necessary. Flexibility to adapt to occasional scheduled video meetings and collaborative tasks is essential.

Positions in this function typically require standing, climbing, balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, crawling, reaching, standing, walking, pushing, pulling, lifting, fingering, grasping, feeling, talking, hearing, seeing and repetitive motions.
Concentrated mental and/or visual attention. The work involves performing complex tasks to very close accuracy and quality specifications, or a high degree of hand and eye coordination for sustained periods.
The job is typically performed under comfortable working conditions; any disagreeable elements are generally absent during normal performance of job.
Compliance with company attendance standards.

Sedentary work involves sitting most of the time. Jobs are sedentary if walking and standing are required only occasionally, and all other sedentary criteria are met.

We Offer

We provide a variety of medical insurance plans, with dental and vision coverage, Employee 401(k), tuition reimbursement, and much more.

At CECO, we are committed to a culture where every employee is valued and respected for their unique experiences and perspectives. We believe a diverse and inclusive work environment contributes to the rich exchange of ideas and diversity of thoughts, that inspires innovation and brings the best solutions to our customers.

About Us

CECO’s Commitment to Our People

At CECO, our people are at the center of everything we do. Whether you’re a professional looking for a career change, an undergraduate student exploring opportunities, or a recent graduate with an advanced degree, you’ll find your chance to make a difference with CECO.

About Ceco

CECO Environmental is a leading environmentally focused, diversified industrial company whose solutions protect people, the environment, and industrial equipment across the globe, serving a broad landscape of industrial air, industrial water and energy transition markets.

We serve these markets and our global customers through our key business segments: Engineered Systems and Industrial Process Solutions. Learn more about CECO by visiting About Us .

new_jobs.description:
The Regional Program Manager (RPM) owns delivery of the ERTS Commercial Compliance Program within an assigned multi-state region. This is a working manager role: the RPM performs client compliance inspections, audits, hazard assessments, and on-site EH&S training while also managing the regional book of business, client relationships, scheduling, subcontractors, and quality of deliverables. The RPM is the primary technical and commercial point of contact for program clients in the region.

The program spans OSHA, EPA, and DOT HMT requirements, plus the state programs that apply in the region. The ideal candidate has a consulting or multi-site practitioner background, is comfortable in a client facing environment, and can translate regulatory findings into practical corrective actions and sellable follow up work.

Clean Harbors is the leading provider of environmental, energy and industrial services throughout the United States, Canada, Mexico and Puerto Rico. Everywhere industry meets environment, Clean Harbors is on-site, providing premier environmental, energy and industrial services. We are solving tough problems through innovation and proven methodology – come be part of the solution with us.

This position is located and supports the Central Region of the US.

Why work for Clean Harbors?

Health and Safety is our #1 priority and we live it 3-6-5!
Focus on maintaining sustainability and cleaning the Earth
Recruiting Pay range of $110,000-$120,000
Comprehensive health benefits coverage after 30 days of full-time employment including 401K with Company match
Own part of the company with our Employee Stock Purchase Plan
Opportunities for growth and development for all the stages of your career
Company paid training and tuition reimbursement

Responsibilities

Program and Client Management

Manage all Commercial Compliance Program accounts in the region: onboarding, annual service calendars, scheduling of site visits, and delivery of services.
Serve as the single point of contact for regional clients; conduct kickoff and close meetings, present findings to leadership, and manage escalations.
Track utilization, billable hours, and deliverable status; maintain accurate client records, inspection reports, training rosters, and corrective action logs.
Coordinate and quality-check subcontractors for specialty scopes.
Identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities and hand off or close in coordination with sales.

Compliance Services

Perform on-site compliance audits and gap analyses against regulatory requirements and best practices.
Conduct hazard assessments including PPE hazard assessments, job hazard analyses, and facility walkthroughs; document findings with regulatory citations, risk ranking, and recommended corrective actions.
Review client hazardous waste program and storage areas: generator category determinations and episodic generation, waste determinations, accumulation area inspections, contingency plan reviews, biennial reports, manifest recordkeeping
Deliver monthly inspection program tools and safety communications ('safety splashes') to program clients.
Support clients during agency inspections and in responding to OSHA citations, EPA or state notices of violation, and consent orders.

Training Delivery

Develop and deliver on-site and virtual EH&S training, including OSHA HAZWOPER and general industry topics, RCRA Hazardous Waste, DOT Hazardous Materials.
Assist clients with maintain training records to satisfy regulatory documentation requirements and support client audit defense.

Regional Regulatory Awareness

Maintain working knowledge of state-plan OSHA programs and state-authorized RCRA programs in the assigned region and advise clients where state requirements are more stringent than federal.
Monitor regulatory changes affecting program clients and brief the Director and client contacts.

Qualifications

Education:

Bachelor’s degree in occupational safety and health, Environmental Science, Industrial Hygiene, Engineering, Chemistry, or a closely related technical field.

Experience

Seven to ten years of progressive EHS experience, including at least three years performing compliance audits or inspections across multiple sites or multiple clients.
Demonstrated hands-on experience with both general industry safety programs (29 CFR 1910) and RCRA hazardous waste generator compliance (40 CFR Parts 260 to 262).
Experience delivering EHS training to hourly and supervisory audiences.
Experience in an environmental or EHS consulting firm, or in a multi-site corporate EHS role with external client or vendor-facing responsibility.

Required Credentials, Training, And Conditions

Valid driver's license and acceptable motor vehicle record; ability to travel 50 to 70 percent, including overnight.
40-Hour HAZWOPER
RCRA training
DOT hazmat employee training
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and web-based EHS data platforms; ability to write clear, citation-supported technical reports.

Preferred Qualifications

Board certification. One or more board certifications: Certified Safety Professional (CSP) or Associate Safety Professional (ASP) from BCSP; Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM) from IHMM; Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH) from BGC; or OHST/CHST from BCSP.
Management systems. ISO 14001 / ISO 45001 lead auditor or internal auditor training; experience with EHS management system audits.
Adjacent programs. Experience with SPCC plans, Tier II reporting, & stormwater (NPDES MSGP).
Advanced degree. Master's degree in related discipline.
Leadership and commercial. Prior experience managing or mentoring field EHS staff; experience scoping and pricing consultation work.

Physical Requirements And Working Conditions

Frequent walking and standing on industrial sites, including outdoor areas, shop floors, loading docks, and container storage areas; ability to climb stairs and ladders and lift up to 40 pounds.
Wear required PPE including safety-toe footwear, eye and hearing protection, and respirators as required.
Extended regional driving and periodic air travel; home office when not in the field.

Description

Prime Video is a first-stop entertainment destination offering customers a vast collection of premium programming in one app available across thousands of devices. Prime members can customize their viewing experience and find their favorite movies, series, documentaries, and live sports – including Amazon MGM Studios-produced series and movies; licensed fan favorites; and programming from Prime Video add-on subscriptions such as Apple TV+, Max, Crunchyroll and MGM+. Are you interested in shaping the future of entertainment? Prime Video's technology teams are creating best-in-class digital video experience.

As a Prime Video technologist, you’ll have end-to-end ownership of the product, user experience, design, and technology required to deliver state-of-the-art experiences for our customers. You’ll get to work on projects that are fast-paced, challenging, and varied. You’ll also be able to experiment with new possibilities, take risks, and collaborate with remarkable people.

We’ll look for you to bring your diverse perspectives, ideas, and skill-sets to make Prime Video even better for our customers. With global opportunities for talented technologists, you can decide where a career Prime Video Tech takes you!

Prime Video is on a mission to reimagine how customers discover and engage with content across the entertainment landscape. As part of this vision, we’re investing heavily in building scalable, science-friendly infrastructure to accelerate the pace of innovation in machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI). We’re seeking a Principal Engineer to lead the technical direction of our next-generation Recommender Systems (RecSys) platforms — systems that sit at the core of how customers experience Prime Video.

Prime Video Personalization and Discovery (PVPD) is dedicated to creating a highly personalized content discovery experience that not only delights our customers but also drives both short-and long-term business goals. Our scope includes personalized recommendations, search, marketing, and the advanced machine learning technology and infrastructure that underpins these experiences. Our mission is to automate and enhance customer engagement through personalization, using ML and Generative AI.

In this role, you will partner closely with applied scientists, product teams, and platform engineers to define and deliver highly extensible systems that fuel personalized discovery at scale. you will lead the technical strategy and architecture of Prime Video’s end-to-end personalization stack — spanning data ingestion, feature engineering, training and serving platform, candidate retrieval, multi-stage ranking, dynamic content grouping, whole page optimization, and orchestration. Your work will shape how millions of customers discover content they love, optimizing for engagement, retention, and long-term customer value.

You will bring clarity to ambiguity, complexity, ROI, planning, and trade-off etc that dramatically improves the agility, usability, and extensibility of our ML solutions. Your technical leadership will shape the future of AI/ML across Prime Video, unlocking generative and ML models that personalize content for hundreds of millions of viewers worldwide.

Consistently meet challenging deadlines and deliver high-quality solutions that enable the Prime Video platform to scale to meet growing customer demand.
Overcome obstacles and persist in the face of setbacks to ensure critical initiatives are successfully completed.
Proactively identify and mitigate risks, communicating regularly with stakeholders on project status and issues.
Demonstrate deep technical expertise in cloud infrastructure, distributed systems, ML/AI fluency and large-scale data processing.

Accountable for the overall strategy and successful execution of large, complex infrastructure optimization and scaling programs.
Partner closely with engineering, product, and business leaders to align initiatives with high-level objectives and achieve measurable improvements in efficiency or customer experience.
Communicate ideas effectively to a wide range of audiences, foster constructive dialogue, and lead the resolution of contentious technical issues.
Set a best-in-class example for project/program management practices, driving crisp decision-making and proactive risk mitigation.

7+ years of technical product or program management experience
5+ years of software development experience
Experience designing or architecting (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems
Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition

new_jobs.description:
Description

Amazon Robotics (AR) seeks a talented and motivated Sr. Technical Program Manager (TPM) to join the Quality Technology Services (QTS) organization, focused on manufacturing technology platforms. This role owns the program management and delivery of manufacturing execution systems and shop-floor technology solutions including Tulip (MES platform), Atlas tools, and associated integrations that enable Amazon Robotics' production operations at scale.

The TPM will lead programs that connect manufacturing operations with technology platforms, driving capability build-out, system implementations, and continuous improvement across Tulip MES, Atlas tools (work instructions, traceability, quality inspection, production dashboards), and their integrations with enterprise systems (ERP, PLM, and supply chain platforms). This is a high-visibility role requiring strong manufacturing domain expertise, technical program management rigor, and the ability to partner with plant operations, manufacturing engineering, quality, and software teams to deliver solutions that improve throughput, quality, and operator experience on the shop floor.

The ideal candidate brings a passion for manufacturing technology transformation, hands-on experience with MES platforms and shop-floor digitization, and the leadership skills to drive cross-functional alignment between manufacturing operations, IT, quality engineering, and partner technology teams within QTS.

Key job responsibilities

Own end-to-end program management for Tulip MES and Atlas manufacturing tools from requirements through deployment and operational handoff across Amazon Robotics manufacturing sites.
Drive the roadmap and capability framework for manufacturing technology solutions: work instructions, production tracking, traceability, quality inspection, and operator-facing applications.
Lead requirements design, process mapping, user acceptance testing, and rollout planning for Tulip apps and Atlas tool deployments in collaboration with manufacturing engineering and plant operations.
Manage integrations between manufacturing execution platforms and boundary systems (ERP/SAP, PLM/Teamcenter, quality systems, data platforms) to ensure end-to-end data flow from shop floor to enterprise.
Partner with manufacturing site teams to understand operational pain points, prioritize technology investments, and drive adoption of digital tools on the production floor.
Coordinate cross-functionally with QTS engineering, quality, supply chain, and infrastructure teams to define technical requirements and deliver integrated solutions.
Establish program governance: status reporting, dependency management, risk mitigation, and executive communication — across concurrent manufacturing technology workstreams.
Drive continuous improvement: measure platform adoption, operator feedback, and production KPIs to iterate on manufacturing technology solutions.
Manage vendor relationships (e.g., Tulip) including feature requests, support escalations, and contract alignment with QTS vendor management.

Job Description

Join a team of development program management professionals to lead Honeywell Aerospace’s development programs within the Engines & Power Systems (E&PS) Strategic Business Group (SBG). You will work directly under the supervision of the Senior Program Director for Power Systems programs. As a Senior Program Manager, you will be expected to execute development programs of significant size and complexity. This involves achieving scope, schedule, cost, delivery, and quality requirements while showcasing mastery in program management skills. A thorough understanding of various workstreams, including functions and Centers of Excellence (COEs), is essential for this role. You will manage and lead complex, global development programs that may span multiple major domestic and international locations. These programs require the coordination of technology development and production across different sites. Your responsibilities include defining, generating, and implementing program plans, as well as ensuring the on-time delivery of milestones for both customers and internal stakeholders.

new_jobs.description:
Title

Technical Program Manager

Belong. Connect. Grow. with KBR!

KBR’s National Security Solutions team provides high-end engineering and advanced technology solutions to our customers in the intelligence and national security communities. In this position, your work will have a profound impact on the country’s most critical role – protecting our national security.

Why Join Us?

Innovative Projects: KBR’s work is at the forefront of engineering, logistics, operations, science, program management, mission IT and cybersecurity solutions.
Collaborative Environment: Be part of a dynamic team that thrives on collaboration and innovation, fostering a supportive and intellectually stimulating workplace.
Impactful Work: Your contributions will be pivotal in designing and optimizing defense systems that ensure national security and shape the future of space defense.

Position Summary

KBR, Inc. is seeking a highly capable technical program manager to join our team in Dayton, OH (on-site). This role supports the Architecture and Systems Engineering (ASE) Group in the development, implementation, and proliferation of mission system Government Reference Architectures (GRAs). These GRAs provide the backbone for enabling advanced sensor capability for emerging and legacy systems across the Air Force, other component services, and international partners. This position serves as a technical program manager performing cost, schedule, performance, and risk management for various contractual activities conducting open system architecture maturation, model-based systems engineering, software development, and system verification & validation. The ideal candidate would have experience in agile development, stakeholder management, and program management.

Key Responsibilities

Manage: Utilize data-driven techniques to guide an industry/government consortium in the maturation, verification, and implementation of GRAs. Program management duties include balancing program cost and schedule factors to drive successful mission outcomes for the Government customer.
Lead: Leads a multi-disciplinary industry and Government team in developing and executing technical and programmatic strategies focused on delivering superior open system architecture products that meet adopter needs. Utilizes adopter feedback to develop easy-to-use Government Reference Architectures and standards.
Engage: Proactively engage with a diverse stakeholder community to ensure user feedback is rapidly and iteratively incorporated into ASE products. Works with stakeholders to formulate collaborative approaches to deliver successful program outcomes.
Deliver: Process owner supporting Agile development of Government Reference Architectures and standards focused on delivering easy to use products and services supporting multiple customers.
Perform: Support the Government customer in developing tactical execution plans based on high-level strategic guidance. Utilize agile management processes to lead an industry consortium in the execution of those plans.
Gap Analysis & Risk Identification: Based on identified system capability gaps, system requirements, and stakeholder feedback, formulate and implement executable program strategies that deliver high-quality open architecture products. Identify and define suitable risk mitigation plans to address program and/or technical issues.

Work Environment

Location: Onsite
Travel Requirements: 0-10%
Working Hours: Standard – Core hours 0900 - 1500

Qualifications

Required:

Bachelor of Science is a technical field.
Active Top Secret clearance.
3+ years in technical execution.
10+ years of technical program management.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to form strong relationships with team members, customers, and other Government partners.
Strong technical proficiency with a willingness/ability to learn about mission system software architectures.
Work with a team of Government and industry SMEs to ensure that programmatic and technical objectives are met.
Ability to own responsibility for deliverables, cost, and schedule.
Ability to manage workload of simultaneous tasking in a fast paced, high-demand environment.
Personality for a consensus building among multiple stakeholders with competing equities.

Desired

10+ years in technical execution in a software-related discipline.
7+ years of Government acquisition program management
3+ years working in Special Access environments
Familiarity with Agile software development, CI/CD pipelines, and practices.
Familiarity with existing DoD open architectures and standards including Agile Mission Suite (AMS), Open Mission Systems (OMS), Universal Command & Control Interface (UCI), or related open architectures.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If you’re excited about making a significant impact in the field of space defense and working on projects that matter, we encourage you to apply and join our team at KBR. Let's shape the future together.

KBR Benefits

KBR offers a selection of competitive lifestyle benefits which could include 401K plan with company match, medical, dental, vision, life insurance, AD&D, flexible spending account, disability, paid time off, or flexible work schedule. We support career advancement through professional training and development.

Belong, Connect and Grow at KBR

At KBR, we are passionate about our people and our Zero Harm culture. These inform all that we do and are at the heart of our commitment to, and ongoing journey toward being a People First company. That commitment is central to our team of team’s philosophy and fosters an environment where everyone can Belong, Connect and Grow. We Deliver – Together.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, disability, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, veteran status, genetic information, union status and/or beliefs, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

What You Will Do

This position is open for external candidates only to apply.

The Weapons Product Definition (E-11) group is looking for a Science/Engineering Program Manager. E-11 provides model-based system engineering, mechanical design engineering, and computer-aided design (CAD) support to the active stockpile weapons systems, hydrodynamic tests, sub-critical experiments, and related qualification efforts.

The successful candidate will provide leadership and overall management of a large E-11 portfolio that is comprised of work performed for multiple programs, including the B61, W76, W78, W88, and W93. The PM is expected to serve as the primary interface between technical leads and program partners, with the ability to help translate mission needs into well-defined requirements, develop funding estimates, and establish and monitor executable schedules. The role requires building trust and consensus across diverse stakeholders, facilitating negotiations, and maintaining proactive, solutions-oriented communication to ensure strong alignment between technical teams and customers.

Working with E-DO, you will also help with developing robust metrics and reporting frameworks that provide leadership with transparent, data-driven insights into program performance., and You will also implement risk identification, tracking, and reporting methodology that enables proactive mitigation and clear communication of projects health.

This role offers the opportunity to work at the intersection of engineering innovation and strategic program execution, shaping the future of E-11 capabilities.

E-11 Science/Engineering Program Manager key responsibilities:

Gathering status reports across all E-11 projects from FLMs, team leads, projects leads and individual designers and engineers
Serving as an effective liaison on projects' scope/schedule/resources/budget between E-11 personnel and stakeholders
Attending weekly Integrated Schedule meetings
Tracking budgets and work package deliverables throughout the current fiscal year
Working with customers and E-11 staff to develop and finalize work packages for the upcoming fiscal year
Coordinating with the group's budget analyst on a weekly basis to proactively address any budget concerns, update staff forecasts, and maintain a close working relationship
Tracking new design requests and working closely with FLMs to ensure their timely assignments
Assisting with metric data collection and analysis
Assisting with procurement tracking, working closely with vendors, E-11 personnel and programs
Assisting with contract tracking

What You Need

Minimum Job Requirements:

Program Management:

Knowledge and experience in program management including:

Defining program work scope, schedules, budgets, priorities, and performance milestones;
Developing cost, scope and schedule baselines;
Reporting cost and schedule variance; and
Managing change control and risk
The capacity to work independently with minimum supervision, as well as the ability to be an effective member of a multidisciplinary team is expected.

Technical Skills:

Ability to understand technical concepts related to E-11 capabilities and customer requirements within the portfolios you support

Collaboration:

Demonstrated effective oral and written communication skills, e.g. formal / informal publications and reports
Ability to serve as the primary spokesperson for a program, reporting status and proactively informing stakeholders of any issues

Process Improvements:

Demonstrated ability to identify, design, and implement process improvements that increase efficiency, consistency, and program outcomes for internal employees, customers and leaders

Ability to obtain a DOE Q clearance, which usually requires US citizenship

Education and Experience:
Position requires a bachelor's degree in a related field from an accredited institution and 5 years of directly related experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience directly related to the occupation.

Desired Qualifications:

Formal project or program management training or certification (e.g., PMP)
Familiarity with MicroStrategy, CRES, Synthesis, pivot tables
Experience supporting DOE/NNSA programs or interacting with federal stakeholders
Active DOE or DoD Security Clearance
Active Sigma-15
Demonstrated initiative in identifying and implementing business process improvements.

Work Location:
The work location for this position is onsite and located in Los Alamos, NM. All work locations are at the discretion of management.

Position commitment:

Regular appointment employees are required to serve a period of continuous service in their current position in order to be eligible to apply for posted jobs throughout the Laboratory. If an employee has not served the time required, they may only apply for Laboratory jobs with the documented approval of their Division Leader. The position commitment for this position is 1 year.

Note to Applicants:

Along with your resume, please include a detailed cover letter explaining how you meet each of the minimum requirements and any of the desired qualifications

Due to federal restrictions contained in the current National Defense Authorization Act, citizens of the People's Republic of China-including the special administrative regions of Hong Kong and Macau-as well as citizens of the Islamic Republic of Iran, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea), and the Russian Federation, who are not Lawful Permanent Residents ("green card" holders) are prohibited from accessing facilities that support the mission, functions, and operations of national security laboratories and nuclear weapons production facilities, which includes Los Alamos National Laboratory.

Where You Will Work

Located in beautiful northern New Mexico, Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) is a multidisciplinary research institution engaged in strategic science on behalf of national security. Our generous benefits package includes:

PPO or High Deductible medical insurance with the same large nationwide network
Dental and vision insurance
Free basic life and disability insurance
Paid childbirth and parental leave
Award-winning 401(k) (6% matching plus 3.5% annually)
Learning opportunities and tuition assistance
Flexible schedules and time off (PTO and holidays)
Onsite gyms and wellness programs
Extensive relocation packages (outside a 50 mile radius)

Additional Details

Directive 206.2
- Employment with Triad requires a favorable decision by NNSA indicating employee is suitable under NNSA Supplemental Directive 206.2. Please note that this requirement applies only to citizens of the United States. Foreign nationals are subject to a similar requirement under DOE Order 142.3A.

Clearance:
Q
(Position will be cleared to this level). Selected applicants will be subject to a background investigation conducted by or on behalf of the Federal Government, and must meet eligibility requirements* for access to classified matter. This position requires a Q clearance, and obtaining such clearance requires US Citizenship except in extremely rare circumstances. Dependent upon the position, additional authorization to access classified information may be required, which may or may not be available to dual citizens. Receipt of a Q clearance and additional access authorization ultimately is a decision of the Federal Government and not of Triad.

Eligibility requirements: To obtain a clearance, an individual must be at least 18 years of age; U.S. citizenship is required except in very limited circumstances. See DOE Order 472.2 for additional information.

New-Employment Drug Test:
The Laboratory requires successful applicants to complete a new-employment drug test and maintains a substance abuse policy that includes random drug testing. Although New Mexico and other states have legalized the use of marijuana, use and possession of marijuana remain illegal under federal law. A positive drug test for marijuana will result in termination of employment, even if the use was pre-offer.

Equal Opportunity:
Los Alamos National Laboratory is an equal opportunity employer. All employment practices are based on qualification and merit, without regard to protected categories such as race, color, national origin, ancestry, religion, age, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status or spousal affiliation, physical or mental disability, medical conditions, pregnancy, status as a protected veteran, genetic information, or citizenship within the limits imposed by federal, state, and local laws and regulations. The Laboratory is also committed to making our workplace accessible to individuals with disabilities and will provide reasonable accommodations, upon request, for individuals to participate in the application and hiring process. To request such an accommodation, please send an email to applyhelp@lanl.gov or call (505)-664-6947.

Use your unique talents and make an immediate impact…

This individual should be a self-motivated professional with experience leading high performing enterprise operations teams in a high op-temp, top secret environment. Within the CESO program, the Defense Information System Agency (DISA) is looking to ensure highly reliable delivery of critical secure information capabilities in support of senior DoD and IC community leaders. As part of this task order, Leidos manages the operations and sustainment of the cloud and broader information environment to include operational engineering, support to the continuous development & continuous integration environment, fourth estate consolidation, and broad professional services – ITIL/DevSecOps based processes, excellent customer experience 1st call resolution, and service catalog-based delivery for Defense Working Capital Fund (DWCF) Model.

HS2 Ltd endeavours to ensure everyone working for us and with us feels included, thrives, and achieves their full potential. In practice, this means we are positive and inclusive about making adjustments, providing flexible working, encouraging our staff networks to flourish, and providing personal and professional development opportunities.

As a Senior Project Manager
at HS2 you will be responsible for leading multidisciplinary teams to manage the resolution of cross-programme risks and issues, coordinating diverse teams to develop integrated solutions for formal governance approvals, interface with external stakeholders whilst working collaboratively with internal delivery and functional teams. This role will work collaboratively with the Supply Chain to enable the efficient delivery of Washwood Heath to budget, time and quality and support the successful delivery of the whole HS2 railway into passenger service.

About The Role

To be responsible for supporting the Washwood Heath Area Director to deliver integration capability for Washwood Heath, working closely with the Construction JV, Programme Integration Unit, functional and stakeholder structures and delivering in line with HS2’s integration behaviours and ways of working.
To be embedded within the Washwood Heath area and supporting the Director to effectively and efficiently manage integration risks and issues.
To be responsible for leading a team of Project Managers.
To be responsible for enabling, taking, and recommending best for programme decisions, to ensure successful delivery of the whole Systems programme.
To be responsible for managing and working with a wide range of internal (to HS2) and external stakeholders to identify and resolve integration challenges. These will range from the Civils Integration Unit, Systems Delivery Integration Unit, Operations and Maintenance, matrix functions such as the PMO, Commercial, Engineering and IM, Main Contractors and Designers, through to external stakeholders such as DfT, ORR, HSE, Fire Authorities, Utilities Companies, Network Rail and TfL
To be responsible for horizon scanning for integration risks and opportunities and escalating to the Programme Integration Unit so that Phase level contingency is allocated appropriately and presents value for money.
To support the planning and execution of Systems Handovers and Transitions ultimately supporting the delivery of an integrated HS2 Railway into passenger service.
To be responsible for reviewing and challenging programme schedules, looking at cross-HS2 dependencies to optimise delivery.
To be responsible for supporting a collaborative culture which enables high performance by encouraging innovation and knowledge sharing between HS2 as the client, other Integrated Project Teams, and the supply chain.

Actively promote and embed Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI) in all your work and support and comply with all organisational initiatives, policies, and procedures on EDI.

Influencing & Negotiating – the ability to influence and negotiate with internal functions and external supply chain partners.
Building Relationships – Ability to establish and maintain relationships with internal and external stakeholders and suppliers to resolve emergent risk situations.

Knowledge

Understanding of the project management knowledge aligned to the level of APM Project Manager (advanced)
Understanding of the technical elements and architecture of the relevant scope of work within the overall HS2 programme, including interdependencies.
Understanding of the nature of the relevant contract structures and the design and application of appropriate contract and supplier performance systems.
Understanding of risk identification and management
Understanding of project schedule management, dependencies, and risk assessment

Types of Experience

Experience of the entire project lifecycle including planning, procuring, developing, and implementing project activities.
Experience of testing and commissioning across complex technical integration projects.
Experience of handing over operational assets to the end-user and the suite of requirements
Experience of leading, managing people and working across functions and disciplines to deliver complex objectives.
Degree level qualification in project management, engineering, commercial management, or the equivalent experience.

new_jobs.description:
Description

The Amazon Aviation Security (AvSec) team is seeking an enthusiastic AvSec Manager to provide leadership, and oversight for Amazon Air’s (AIR) cargo transportation business. The AvSec Manager will be responsible for defining and driving new initiatives for the transportation supply chain involving Amazon owned and third-party (3P) delivery methods. This includes independently determining risk-based security standards, exercising discretion in interpreting and applying airport and federal regulations, and making decisions regarding compliance approaches and standardized processes. The AvSec Manager serves as the interface between AIR and AvSec leadership, and will be responsible for exercising independent judgment in identifying, reporting, and leading the correction of non-compliances and deficiencies. The successful candidate will serve as a point of contact for regulatory engagement, lead the correction of non-compliance with established security policies and procedures, and develop and improve processes to ensure operational integrity, owning goals and performance targets for their respective region.

The AvSec Manager supports the AIR operation program as the subject matter expert on interpreting, implementing, and validating security requirements, to ensure associates, 3P vendors, visitors, and assets (people, property, and data) are secure and the organization is prepared to properly respond to various security related incidents. The candidate must have a demonstrated ability to exercise independent judgement, utilize their security expertise and management strength to challenge conventional wisdom, think strategically, and communicate effectively.

Key job responsibilities

The AvSec Manager’s responsibilities include prioritizing team resources and tasks in order to meet AvSec’s targets and goals in an ambiguous environment. This position will lead the business to meet aviation security best practices, regulatory compliance, serving as a subject matter expert in aviation security. This position has a key role in hiring and developing the right workforce strategy to meet long-term process targets.

The AvSec Manager’s responsibilities also include identifying and analyzing gaps in compliance with security procedures and regulatory standards, physical security design standards and policies and leading Security Management Systems (SeMS) processes for risk mitigation. Additional responsibilities include developing new and evaluating existing security standards by establishing workflows, Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and operational excellence mechanisms to ensure customer outcomes are data driven, measured and validated.

This is a new and evolving business operation, and AvSec is looking for someone who can introduce best practices and grow as the team’s scale and scope expand.

Additional Responsibilities Include

Set and clarify requirements and expectations with associates and leadership at each facility.
Create security and quality initiatives that continuously improve processes and mitigate deficiencies.
Provide job-specific training to associates and oversee staffing qualifications and ensure required levels are maintained.
Work closely with site leaders and support staff to ensure on-going support for AIR security initiatives and policies.
Work closely with AIR regional leadership and 3P service providers.
Manage timely, ethical, and professional investigations into security incidents and violations.
Serve as Amazon’s representative for Transportation Security Administration (TSA) inspections and inquiries; investigate allegations of regulatory violations and mitigate regulatory enforcement.
Utilize Security Management Systems (SeMS) to identify the root cause for failures and develop mitigating actions to reduce risk.
Conduct visits, assessments, and audits of processes and records.
Implement security and shrinkage control programs to protect assets from loss due to internal/external theft and operational issues.
This role covers a 24/7 operation and you must be able to work all shifts, including nights, weekends and holidays shifts as necessary.

The Span of Authority for this role includes oversite of a single facility within a geographic region. This will include the hiring and development of team members, supporting operational leadership, managing difficult problems, mitigating immediate risks and deciding if escalation is required.

Eligibility Qualifications

This role is regulated by the TSA and is subject to requirements imposed by the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) because the role will require access to U.S. CBP-regulated areas. Successful candidates must therefore complete all screenings prescribed by the TSA and the U.S. CBP.
Individuals hired into this position will have unescorted access privileges to airport security identification display areas (SIDA). For this reason, eligibility for this role will be limited to individuals who pass a security screening, as required by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Department of Homeland Security (DHS), and TSA (as applicable).
This position may be subject to Department of Transportation (DOT) drug and alcohol testing. Federal law requires Amazon to determine an applicant's history of DOT drug and/or alcohol violation(s) or refusal(s) to test before hiring applicant into a safety-sensitive position.
This position requires an employee’s full and unimpaired skills and judgment to safely execute their job duties to ensure the safety and security of Amazon AIR personnel, third-party contractors, Airport personnel, cargo, and equipment. This position is therefore designated as a safety sensitive position and is subject to mandatory pre-employment and, where permitted, post-hire drug testing.

A day in the life

The AvSec Manager will ensure the security of Amazon's associates, assets and data at an AIR Cargo facility. You will lead site compliance with TSA regulations, Amazon Policies and Procedures, and local regulations. A successful candidate will leverage their subject matter expertise to assess brand and regulatory risk factors and evaluate opportunities to improve compliance and mitigate discovered risks. You will use independent judgment to investigate cases that would expose the company to regulatory risk, and make recommendations based on an assessment of the risk. This includes developing and driving engagement strategies for Amazon associates and leaders, to drive compliance. A successful candidate will become a subject matter expert on site security infrastructure, policies and procedures, and regulatory compliance. AvSec is a liaison with any law enforcement or government/regulatory officials that visit the site.

Beyond day-to-day operations, you'll contribute to strategic security initiatives. You'll analyze incident trends to identify systemic issues, participate in regional security planning discussions, provide input on policy development, and help shape AvSec's approach to emerging aviation security challenges. This role provides a pathway to develop strategic thinking skills while maintaining strong tactical execution.

About The Team

The AvSec team is responsible for security, loss prevention, and regulatory compliance at Amazon. The organization is built with four core pillars; Security Management Systems, Programs and Quality Assurance, Security Operations, and Credentialing. The organization is committed to identifying and mitigating risk to people, Amazon assets, Amazon brand and regulatory compliance through the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of best-in-class aviation security procedures, standards and guardrails between which Amazon operates. By supporting our customer teams at fulfillment centers and AIR sites to implement process improvements, mitigate risk, resolve equipment issues, and implement new processes to improve performance, AvSec contributes to safe and secure transportation of air cargo to our customers.

Basic Qualifications

4+ years of compliance program management, legal, governance, audit, risk/loss prevention, or equivalent experience
3+ years of managing food safety and quality in a large-scale retail or manufacturing environment experience
Bachelor's degree in Food Science or related field
Knowledge of retail food code and regulations governing grocery retail at local, state, and federal levels
Bachelor's degree or equivalent
Experience handling confidential information
Experience interacting with local food safety regulators
3+ years of experience in a security or investigations related field or related Bachelor degree.

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of program requirements definition and data and metrics leveraging to drive improvements experience
Professional auditing qualification, or similar risk or compliance credentials
Experience with SQL and Excel
Analytical leader experienced in performance based, action and results-oriented management, strong project manager and effective problem solver.
Ability to assess risks and challenge current practices to develop and deliver innovative solutions to meet or exceed the customer expectations.
Business Continuity experience.

Position Overview

The Information Management Program Manager provides senior leadership for Kiewit’s Industrial District Project Information Management (PIM) Program and Information Management/Document Control organization. This role is responsible for building and leading a high-performing information management function that supports project execution, strengthens governance, develops talent, and drives consistent information practices across the industrial market.

This position partners with engineering and operations leadership, functional leaders, and project teams to standardize execution, improve processes, align systems and workflows, and ensure project information is controlled from startup through final turnover and closeout.

District Overview

Kiewit’s Industrial District delivers complex construction and engineering projects across North America, including advanced technology, power, industrial, and other large-scale markets. Our teams operate in fast-paced project environments that require disciplined execution, strong coordination, and reliable information management. This role is key to helping project teams establish the standards, systems, and controls needed to manage project information effectively throughout the full project lifecycle.

Location

This position may be based in a district or area office, depending on business needs. Candidates must be willing to travel as required to support project assignments.

Responsibilities

District Leadership & Program Ownership

Serve as the district leader and primary champion for the Project Information Management Program.
Lead development, deployment, and continuous improvement of district PIM standards, procedures, playbooks, tools, and assurance processes.
Influence operations, functional leaders, and project teams to align information management requirements with project needs and delivery models.
Establish district-wide governance, metrics, reporting requirements, and assurance processes.
Drive consistency across engineering, procurement, construction, startup, commissioning, turnover, and final records management.
Lead staffing projections, recruiting support, resource planning, and project deployment strategy for Information Management/Document Control personnel.
Develop talent through onboarding, mentoring, career development, succession planning, and leadership coaching.

Project Startup, Implementation & Governance

Support implementation of Engineering Information Management, Trade Partner Information Management (TPIM), Vendor Data Management, and Turnover Information Management programs.

Information Lifecycle, Turnover & Closeout

Establish governance for engineering information, vendor data, trade partner information, submittals, RFIs, design changes, quality records, commissioning records, turnover packages, final records, and archives.
Strengthen information handoffs from Construction and Quality through completions, commissioning, turnover, client deliverables, and archive.

Trade Partner Information Management

Lead district deployment of Trade Partner Information Management (TPIM) standards and practices.
Establish governance for trade partner submittals, vendor data, design-assist deliverables, delegated design information, quality documentation, and turnover requirements.
Translate client and contract documentation requirements into RFQ, subcontract, vendor, quality, turnover, and final records expectations.
Support pre-award evaluation and onboarding of Trade Partners around systems, submittals, RFIs, quality documentation, delegated design, and turnover requirements.

Systems, Technology & Reporting

Partner with business technology, systems administrators, and project teams to establish systems-of-record and platform governance.
Drive standardization of metadata, numbering, workflows, templates, reporting, and dashboards.
Lead implementation, governance, and optimization of InEight, TeamBinder, SharePoint, Procore, CxAlloy, Power BI, and other approved information platforms.
Develop district metrics and executive dashboards for information readiness, compliance, submittal performance, vendor data, change management, turnover readiness, and final records completion.

Team Development, Assurance & Continuous Improvement

Build team capability through onboarding, training, mentoring, career development, and succession planning.
Evaluate emerging industry trends and delivery models and recommend improvements to district standards.

Required

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Project Controls, Information Management, Business, or a related field.
10+ years of experience supporting large EPC, industrial, power, mining, data center, or advanced technology projects.
Experience in one or more of the following disciplines:
Project Controls
Document Control
Information Management
Engineering Management
Construction Management
Quality Management
Turnover Management
Demonstrated ability to lead teams, influence senior stakeholders, and drive organizational change in complex project environments.
Experience with staffing strategy, recruiting support, team development, onboarding, training, mentoring, or succession planning.
Strong understanding of project delivery lifecycles and interface management.

Preferred

Experience developing standards, procedures, and governance frameworks.
Experience with InEight, TeamBinder, SharePoint, Procore, Power BI, completions/commissioning platforms such as CxAlloy, or similar information management systems.
Experience with Trade Partner Information Management, Vendor Data Management, Quality documentation, and Turnover programs.
Experience translating client, contract, vendor, quality, completions, commissioning, and turnover requirements into execution and Trade Partner requirements.
Experience supporting EPC, Design-Build, Advanced Technology, or complex mega-projects.

new_jobs.title: Security Operations Manager, GSOC, Worldwide Operations Security (WWOS)
new_jobs.description:
Description

The Worldwide Operations Security (WWOS) Global Security Operations Center (GSOC) is Amazon’s 24/7 centralized command center supporting Worldwide Amazon Stores. The GSOC manages critical incidents impacting life safety, operational continuity, and brand reputation by connecting sites with the appropriate subject matter experts and coordinating end-to-end incident response. We accomplish this by creating policy and implementation guidelines; training leadership and staff; using technology to eliminate subjectivity, complexity, and variation; identifying, preparing for, and mitigating risk; and auditing our practices to ensure compliance.

The Security Operations Manager, Global Security Operations Center (GSOC) will provides critical support and timely notification to global partners regarding incidents that have impacted, or have the potential to impact, Life Safety, Operations, and/or the Amazon Brand. They will assist in managerial ownership of their shift and be responsible for ensuring performance SLAs are met, that responses are appropriate according to policies and procedures, and for developing and motivating a highly performant staff. The Security Operations Manager must also deal effectively with ambiguity and make response-related decisions sometimes with incomplete information in the best interest of Amazon.

The successful candidate must have a proven record of effective leadership capabilities and demonstrate elevated judgment while operating under pressure. They must possess the ability to operate autonomously, use discretion when dealing with sensitive and critical information, and apply sound business principles to identify barriers and initiate actions to resolve. The candidate should possess a proven record of working across multiple organizations to resolve escalations where the problem and solutions, as well as risk strategy, may not be well defined.

The GSOC is a 24/7/365 operation, and this position will require shift work, including night and weekend shifts.

Key job responsibilities

Lead 24/7 GSOC shift operations, ensuring timely triage, escalation, and resolution of incidents impacting life safety, operational continuity, and Amazon’s brand.
Provide timely notifications, situation reports, and executive briefings to global stakeholders
Ensure shift operational excellence by maintaining ownership of performance, achieving established Service Level Agreements (SLAs), and driving consistent execution of policies and procedures
Partner with Security, Operations, HR, Workplace Health & Safety (WHS), Legal, Communications and other internal stakeholders to coordinate effective incident response and business continuity support.
Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team of Operations Security Specialists by setting clear expectations, providing regular coaching and feedback, and fostering a culture of accountability, operational excellence, and continuous learning.
Monitor incident trends, operational metrics, and emerging risks to identify opportunities for process improvements, strengthen response capabilities, and reduce recurring issues.
Lead post-incident reviews and drive corrective actions that improve operational resilience, standardize best practices, and enhance the effectiveness of global incident management.
Partner with cross-functional and global teams to develop, implement, and continuously improve processes, tools, and operational standards that support scalable, efficient GSOC operations.
Maintain the highest standards of professionalism, sound judgment, confidentiality, and customer obsession while protecting Amazon’s associates, operations, and brand.

A day in the life

As a GSOC Security Operations Manager, you will lead a team responsible for managing critical security and operational incidents across Amazon’s global network. Your day may include directing responses to workplace emergencies, severe weather events, security threats, transportation incidents, or operational disruptions while coordinating with multiple business partners and executive stakeholders. You will coach your team in real time, provide strategic guidance during escalations, ensure operational metrics are met, and continuously improve processes that strengthen Amazon’s global incident management capability.

Basic Qualifications

7+ years of conducting workplace risk investigations experience
Experience in conducting workplace risk investigations
Experience leveraging technology to drive process improvements
Experience managing direct reports
Bachelor's degree or equivalent

Preferred Qualifications

Partner with data governance, architecture, security, and business teams to improve the trust, accessibility, and appropriate use of information.
Drive adoption, data literacy, and a self-service analytics culture while maintaining appropriate controls and stewardship.

Ensure insights are communicated clearly, with appropriate context, to support decisions, identify trends, and highlight opportunities and risks.

Lead a community of practice to strengthen collaboration, standards, and adoption.

Technology, Data Quality, and Controls

Ensure solutions meet expectations for performance, scalability, usability, resilience, security, and maintainability.
Implement quality controls for data validation, reconciliation, access, change management, and production monitoring.
Set review and validation standards for AI-assisted development and AI-generated insights so that outputs remain accurate, explainable, and auditable.
Partner with data engineering and architecture teams on source integration, platform enhancements, and reusable data products.

Your Skills And Abilities Should Include

Progressive experience in business intelligence, reporting, analytics, or data engineering, including leadership of teams and complex delivery portfolios.
Demonstrated ability to lead managers, engineers, or analysts and to build a high-performing, service-oriented team.

H-E-B is one of the largest, independently owned food retailers in the nation, operating over 380 stores throughout Texas and Mexico, with annual sales generating over $43 billion. H-E-B has led the way with creative new concepts and outstanding service. Our Customer Insights team ensures the voice of the customer and Partner is represented throughout the organization everyday by using qualitative and quantitative research, geospatial insights, analytics, and sensory research. for Own Brand, you’ll work cross-functionally with the Own Brand (private label) and Merchant organization to design, execute, and analyze quantitative consumer research studies that inform brand, product, and design of our world-class private label product portfolio. Regular exposure to or first-hand experience with qualitative research / mixed methodologies

Experience with Sawtooth Software, Qualtrics, or other survey tools is a plus

This desk covers a portfolio of corporate and financial issuers, tracking their credit profile, capital structure and covenant headroom, and feeding that analysis into the rating views and internal credit opinions used across lending, trading and risk functions. The work sits close to real decisions: a stale credit view here can show up as a mispriced position or a missed covenant breach somewhere else in the bank.
How a rating call gets made

Building and maintaining financial models for covered issuers, including leverage, coverage and liquidity metrics
Tracking covenant compliance, rating actions and credit events across the assigned portfolio
Drafting credit notes and issuer updates that summarise financial performance against thesis and triggers
Supporting senior analysts on new issuer onboarding, including first-pass credit write-ups
Monitoring macro, sector and regulatory developments that could move an issuer's credit profile

What we're looking for in a first read

2 to 6 years of experience in credit research, corporate ratings, fixed income research or related credit analysis, with strong financial modelling skills and comfort reading financial statements, indentures and credit agreements. You should be able to write a credit note that a senior analyst can sign off on with minimal rework, and be precise about assumptions in a leverage or coverage model.
Where the seat sits

The role is based out of Mumbai, Bengaluru, Delhi NCR, Hyderabad or Pune, or Remote (India), working alongside a global credit research function with regular touchpoints across time zones.
After you apply

The process includes an HR Screening, a modelling or case assignment, a Technical Round with the credit team and a final Culture Fit conversation. One application here covers this opening and any other Flexiple-matched role that fits your experience, so there is no need to reapply.

About The Role

The Manufacturing Data Analyst plays a critical role in transforming raw manufacturing data into actionable insights that drive operational efficiency and product quality improvements. This position involves analyzing complex datasets from production lines, identifying trends, and providing data-driven recommendations to optimize manufacturing processes. The analyst collaborates closely with engineering, quality assurance, and production teams to support continuous improvement initiatives and reduce waste. By leveraging advanced analytical techniques and tools, the role ensures that manufacturing decisions are supported by accurate and timely data. Ultimately, the Manufacturing Data Analyst contributes to enhancing overall manufacturing performance and competitiveness in the market.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related field.
Proficiency in data analysis tools such as SQL, Excel, and statistical software (e.g., R, Python).
Experience working with manufacturing data or in a manufacturing environment.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail.
Excellent communication skills to effectively convey complex data insights to non-technical stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in a relevant field or equivalent work experience.
Familiarity with manufacturing execution systems (MES) and enterprise resource planning (ERP) software.
Experience with data visualization tools such as Tableau, Power BI, or similar platforms.
Knowledge of Six Sigma, Lean Manufacturing, or other continuous improvement methodologies.
Programming experience in Python or R for advanced data analysis and automation.

Responsibilities

Collect, clean, and analyze manufacturing data from various sources including production equipment, sensors, and enterprise systems.
Develop and maintain dashboards and reports to monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) related to production efficiency, quality, and downtime.
Identify patterns, anomalies, and root causes of manufacturing issues through statistical analysis and data mining techniques.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to design experiments and pilot projects aimed at process optimization and defect reduction.
Present findings and actionable insights to stakeholders through clear visualizations and detailed reports to support decision-making.

Skills

The Manufacturing Data Analyst uses required skills such as SQL and Excel daily to extract and manipulate large datasets from manufacturing systems, ensuring data accuracy and completeness. Statistical software like R or Python is employed to perform in-depth analyses, identify trends, and build predictive models that inform process improvements. Communication skills are essential for translating complex analytical results into clear, actionable insights that can be understood by production and management teams. Preferred skills like familiarity with MES and ERP systems enhance the analyst’s ability to integrate data from multiple sources, providing a comprehensive view of manufacturing operations. Additionally, expertise in data visualization tools allows the analyst to create intuitive dashboards that facilitate real-time monitoring and decision-making.

Description

Prime Video is a first-stop entertainment destination offering customers a vast collection of premium programming in one app available across thousands of devices. Prime members can customize their viewing experience and find their favorite movies, series, documentaries, and live sports – including Amazon MGM Studios-produced series and movies; licensed fan favorites; and programming from Prime Video add-on subscriptions such as Apple TV+, Max, Crunchyroll and MGM+. All customers, regardless of whether they have a Prime membership or not, can rent or buy titles via the Prime Video Store, and can enjoy even more content for free with ads.

Are you interested in shaping the future of entertainment? Prime Video's technology teams are creating best-in-class digital video experience.

As a Prime Video technologist, you’ll have end-to-end ownership of the product, user experience, design, and technology required to deliver state-of-the-art experiences for our customers. You’ll get to work on projects that are fast-paced, challenging, and varied. You’ll also be able to experiment with new possibilities, take risks, and collaborate with remarkable people.

We’ll look for you to bring your diverse perspectives, ideas, and skill-sets to make Prime Video even better for our customers. With global opportunities for talented technologists, you can decide where a career Prime Video Tech takes you!

Prime Video is on a mission to reimagine how customers discover and engage with content across the entertainment landscape. As part of this vision, we’re investing heavily in building scalable, science-friendly infrastructure to accelerate the pace of innovation in machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI). We’re seeking a Principal Engineer to lead the technical direction of our next-generation Recommender Systems (RecSys) platforms — systems that sit at the core of how customers experience Prime Video.

About The Team

Prime Video Personalization and Discovery (PVPD) is dedicated to creating a highly personalized content discovery experience that not only delights our customers but also drives both short-and long-term business goals. Our scope includes personalized recommendations, search, marketing, and the advanced machine learning technology and infrastructure that underpins these experiences. Our mission is to automate and enhance customer engagement through personalization, using ML and Generative AI.

Key Job Responsibilities

In this role, you will partner closely with applied scientists, product teams, and platform engineers to define and deliver highly extensible systems that fuel personalized discovery at scale. you will lead the technical strategy and architecture of Prime Video’s end-to-end personalization stack — spanning data ingestion, feature engineering, training and serving platform, candidate retrieval, multi-stage ranking, dynamic content grouping, whole page optimization, and orchestration. Your work will shape how millions of customers discover content they love, optimizing for engagement, retention, and long-term customer value.

You will bring clarity to ambiguity, complexity, ROI, planning, and trade-off etc that dramatically improves the agility, usability, and extensibility of our ML solutions. Your technical leadership will shape the future of AI/ML across Prime Video, unlocking generative and ML models that personalize content for hundreds of millions of viewers worldwide.

Key job responsibilities

Consistently meet challenging deadlines and deliver high-quality solutions that enable the Prime Video platform to scale to meet growing customer demand.
Overcome obstacles and persist in the face of setbacks to ensure critical initiatives are successfully completed.
Proactively identify and mitigate risks, communicating regularly with stakeholders on project status and issues.
Demonstrate deep technical expertise in cloud infrastructure, distributed systems, ML/AI fluency and large-scale data processing.
Understand the architecture and design limitations of the existing Prime Video systems, ML models, and drive technical decisions that address deficiencies and optimize performance.
Use data-driven analysis to make a compelling case for project priorities and resource allocation.
Accountable for the overall strategy and successful execution of large, complex infrastructure optimization and scaling programs.
Partner closely with engineering, product, and business leaders to align initiatives with high-level objectives and achieve measurable improvements in efficiency or customer experience.
Communicate ideas effectively to a wide range of audiences, foster constructive dialogue, and lead the resolution of contentious technical issues.
Set a best-in-class example for project/program management practices, driving crisp decision-making and proactive risk mitigation.

Basic Qualifications

7+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
7+ years of technical product or program management experience
5+ years of software development experience
Experience designing or architecting (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems
Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition

Preferred Qualifications

8+ years of hands-on work managing complex technology projects experience
Experience managing projects across cross functional teams, building sustainable processes and coordinating release schedules

Lumen is the trusted network for the AI‑powered world, connecting people, data, and applications through our expansive fiber network and connected ecosystem. We enable secure, high‑performance connectivity across cloud, edge, and AI workloads for enterprises, governments, and communities.

At Lumen, you’ll work on infrastructure customers rely on today and build for what’s next, where performance, security, and resilience matter.

This is a high accountability environment where bold ideas drive real innovation for our customers, partners, and industry. The work is challenging, expectations are clear, and trust is built into how we operate. If you’re ready to take ownership, deliver meaningful impact, and help shape the future of AI‑ready connectivity, join us today.

The Role

The HR Knowledge and Intelligence Manager owns the structure, governance, quality, and continuous improvement of HR knowledge across the enterprise. This role helps transform fragmented HR content, policy guidance, process information, decisions, and institutional expertise into trusted knowledge that employees, leaders, HR professionals, and approved AI agents can find and apply with confidence.

Work Location

This is a remote opportunity open to candidates located anywhere in the U.S.

The Main Responsibilities

Define and maintain the HR knowledge and intelligence strategy, roadmap, operating model, governance approach, and success measures aligned to HR priorities and enterprise AI direction.
Create order from fragmented HR knowledge by leading discovery, inventory, taxonomy, metadata, source-of-truth, ownership, and lifecycle standards across approved repositories and systems.
Identify and coordinate resolution of duplicate, outdated, conflicting, incomplete, inaccessible, or ownerless content with the appropriate HR domain owners.
Build and manage a coordinated HR knowledge agent workforce, including agent purpose, work boundaries, instructions, queues, access, quality expectations, escalation paths, and controls.
Partner with HR, AI, technology, legal, privacy, security, data, communications, and records-management teams to make HR knowledge reliable, discoverable, governed, and ready for responsible AI use.
Design functional readiness and quality tests to confirm agents retrieve authoritative sources, preserve context, recognize exceptions, cite evidence where required, and escalate appropriately.
Establish a balanced scorecard for knowledge coverage, ownership, freshness, findability, duplication, conflict resolution, retrieval quality, user outcomes, and agent performance.
Drive adoption of clear, accessible, plain-language HR knowledge practices while preserving policy precision, confidentiality, legal meaning, and local or workforce-specific variation.

What We Look For In a Candidate

Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
7+ years of progressive experience in knowledge management, content strategy, information architecture, HR operations, HR service delivery, governance, organizational learning, or a related discipline.
3+ years leading a complex cross-functional capability, program, or body of work with accountability for standards, governance, decision-making, and measurable outcomes.
Strong understanding of HR functions, HR operating models, employee services, policy and process ownership, and sensitive employee-related information.
Experience creating taxonomies, metadata standards, source-of-truth models, content standards, governance practices, or knowledge lifecycle controls.
Working fluency with generative AI and AI agents, including defining agent work, setting guardrails, evaluating outputs, identifying failure patterns, and determining when human judgment is required.
Strong written communication, facilitation, stakeholder management, and influencing skills with the ability to align decision makers across functions.
Sound judgment regarding privacy, confidentiality, access, records, legal or regulatory considerations, and responsible AI use.

Experience in a large, complex, highly matrixed, distributed, or regulated organization.
Experience with enterprise HR platforms, employee-service technologies, content-management systems, enterprise search, or collaboration repositories.
